topic: Actors, goals and use case diagrams; include and extend
title: Use cases for a mobile money agent app
instructions:
## Goals, not screens

A mobile money **agent** registers customers, performs cash-in and cash-out, and views a float balance. A **customer** sends money and buys airtime. Every money-moving use case (cash-in, cash-out, send money, buy airtime) **includes** "Verify PIN". Cash-out may be **extended** by "Request OTP" when the amount is above a limit. A **supervisor** is a special kind of agent who can also approve float top-ups.

## Do this

Write the diagram: three actors (Supervisor generalises Agent: `Agent <|-- Supervisor`), the use cases, associations, four include relationships to Verify PIN, one extend, and the supervisor's extra use case.

diagram: usecase
actor Agent
actor Customer

diagram: usecase

hints: actor Supervisor then Agent <|-- Supervisor for the generalisation.
Each of CashIn, CashOut, SendMoney and BuyAirtime gets a line like CashIn ..> VerifyPIN : include.
RequestOTP ..> CashOut : extend; the extension points at the base.

checks.label: Supervisor is a kind of Agent

realityNote: Over-using include and extend turns a use case diagram into a flowchart; the rule of thumb is to add them only when the shared behaviour is substantial (PIN verification) or the optional behaviour has its own business rule (OTP above a limit).
